verses.19:12: You shall not swear falsely in My name, nor shall you defile the name of your God. I am the Lord.
verses.19:13: You shall not falsely accuse your neighbor, nor oppress him by force. The wages of your hired worker shall not remain with you until morning.
verses.19:14: You shall not curse a deaf person, nor place a stumbling block before a blind person, but you shall fear the Lord your God, because I am the Lord.
verses.19:15: You shall not do what is unjust, nor judge unjustly. Do not regard the person of the poor, nor honor the face of the powerful. Judge your neighbor justly.
verses.19:16: You shall not be a slanderer nor a whisperer among the people. You shall not stand against the blood of your neighbor. I am the Lord.
verses.19:17: You shall not hate your brother in your heart, but openly reprove him, so that you do not have sin on account of him.
verses.19:18: Do not seek vengeance, nor remember an injury from your fellow citizens. You shall love your friend as yourself. I am the Lord.
verses.19:19: Keep My laws. You shall not make your beast mate with animals of another kind. You shall not sow your field with diverse seed. You shall not be clothed in a garment that is woven from two kinds.
verses.19:20: If a man sleeps with a woman in an intercourse of seed, who is a slave woman even of marriageable age, and yet not redeemed by a price nor granted freedom, both shall be beaten, and they shall not die, because she was not free.
verses.19:21: Now for his offense, he shall offer a ram to the Lord at the entrance of the tabernacle of the testimony,
verses.19:22: and the priest shall pray for him and for his sin before the Lord, and He will be gracious to him again, and the sin will be forgiven.
verses.19:23: When you have entered the land and planted fruit-bearing trees in it, you shall remove their foreskins; the fruits that sprout shall be unclean to you, and you shall not eat from them.
verses.19:24: But in the fourth year, all their produce shall be sanctified, praiseworthy to the Lord.
verses.19:25: And in the fifth year, you shall eat the produce, gathering the fruits that they bring forth. I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:26: You shall not eat with blood. You shall not practice augury, nor observe dreams.
verses.19:27: You shall neither trim your hair in a circle nor shave your beard.
verses.19:28: And over a dead person you shall not cut your flesh, nor make any figures or marks on yourselves. I am the Lord.
verses.19:29: Do not prostitute your daughter, so that the land is not contaminated and filled with wickedness.
verses.19:30: Keep My Sabbaths, and revere My sanctuary. I am the Lord.
verses.19:31: Do not turn aside to magicians, nor inquire anything from soothsayers, so as to be defiled through them. I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:32: Rise up before a gray head, and honor the person of an elderly man, and fear the Lord your God. I am the Lord.
verses.19:33: If a stranger lives in your land and stays among you, do not reproach him,
verses.19:34: but let him be among you as a native, and you shall love him as yourselves, for you also were strangers in the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.
verses.19:35: Do not do anything unjust in judgment, in measuring rule, in weight, in measure.
verses.19:36: Let the balance be just and the weights equal, the modius just and the sextarius equal. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt.
verses.19:37: Keep all My precepts and all the judgments, and do them. I am the Lord.'"
verses.20:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.20:2: "You shall speak these things to the sons of Israel: 'If any man from the sons of Israel, and from the strangers who live in Israel, gives from his seed to the idol Molech, he shall surely die; the people of the land shall stone him.
verses.20:3: And I will set My face against him and will cut him off from the midst of his people, because he has given from his seed to Molech, and has contaminated My sanctuary, and has defiled My holy name.
verses.20:4: And if the people of the land, being negligent and as if thinking little of My command, lets go the man who gave from his seed to Molech, and refuses to kill him,
verses.20:5: I will set My face upon that man and upon his relatives, and I will cut off both him and all who consented with him to commit fornication with Molech from the midst of their people.
verses.20:6: As for the soul that turns aside to magicians and soothsayers and commits fornication with them, I will set My face against it and will destroy it from the midst of its people.
verses.20:7: Sanctify yourselves and be holy, because I am the Lord your God.
verses.20:8: Keep My precepts and do them; I am the Lord who sanctifies you.
verses.20:9: Whoever curses his father or mother shall surely die; he has cursed his father and mother; let his blood be upon him.
verses.20:10: If anyone commits adultery with the wife of another, and perpetrates adultery with the spouse of his neighbor, both the adulterer and the adulteress shall surely die.
verses.20:11: Whoever sleeps with his stepmother and uncovers his father's disgrace, both of them shall surely die; let their blood be upon them.
verses.20:12: If anyone sleeps with his daughter-in-law, both of them shall die, because they have committed wickedness; let their blood be upon them.
verses.20:13: Whoever sleeps with a male in the intercourse of a woman, both of them have committed an abomination; they shall surely die; let their blood be upon them.
verses.20:14: Whoever, in addition to a daughter as his wife, marries her mother has committed wickedness; he shall burn alive with them, and so great an abomination shall not remain in your midst.
verses.20:15: Whoever has intercourse with a beast and a herd animal shall surely die; kill the herd animal as well.
verses.20:16: A woman who lies beneath any beast shall be put to death together with it; let their blood be upon them.
verses.20:17: Whoever takes his sister, his father's daughter or his mother's daughter, and sees her shame, and she looks upon her brother's disgrace, they have committed an abominable thing; they shall be killed in the sight of their people, because they have mutually uncovered their shame, and they shall bear their iniquity.
verses.20:18: Whoever has intercourse with a woman during her menstrual flow and uncovers her shame, and she herself opens the fountain of her blood, both of them shall be destroyed from the midst of their people.
verses.20:19: You shall not uncover the shame of your mother's sister and your father's sister; whoever does this has laid bare the disgrace of his own flesh; both of them shall bear their iniquity.
verses.20:20: Whoever has intercourse with the wife of his paternal uncle or his maternal uncle and uncovers the disgrace of his relatives, both of them shall bear their sin; they shall die without children.
verses.20:21: Whoever marries his brother's wife does an unlawful thing; he has uncovered his brother's shame; they shall be without children.
verses.20:22: Keep My laws and judgments, and do them, so that the land which you are about to enter and inhabit does not vomit you out as well.
verses.20:23: Do not walk in the statutes of the nations that I am about to drive out before you. For they did all these things, and I abhorred them.
verses.20:24: But to you I speak. Possess their land, which I will give to you as an inheritance, a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the Lord your God, who has separated you from the other peoples.
verses.20:25: Therefore you also separate the clean beast from the unclean, and the clean bird from the unclean, so that you do not defile your souls by herd animals, and birds, and all things that move on the earth, and which I have shown to you to be defiled.
verses.20:26: You shall be holy to Me, because I, the Lord, am holy, and I have separated you from the other peoples, so that you would be Mine.
verses.20:27: A man or a woman in whom there is a pythonic spirit or a spirit of divination shall surely die; they shall overwhelm them with stones; let their blood be upon them.'"
verses.21:1: The Lord also said to Moses: "Speak to the priests, the sons of Aaron, and you shall say to them: 'Let a priest not be defiled for the deaths of his fellow citizens,
verses.21:2: except only for blood relatives and close kin, that is, for a father and mother, and a son and daughter, a brother also,
verses.21:3: and a virgin sister who is not married to a man;
verses.21:4: but not even for a ruler of his people shall he be defiled.
verses.21:5: They shall not shave the head nor the beard, nor make cuts in their flesh.
verses.21:6: They shall be holy to their God, and they shall not pollute His name; for they offer the incense of the Lord and the loaves of their God, and therefore they shall be holy.
verses.21:7: They shall not take as a wife a prostitute or a vile woman of prostitution, nor one who has been divorced by her husband, because they are consecrated to their God,
verses.21:8: and they offer the loaves of presentation. Therefore let them be holy, because I also am holy, the Lord who sanctifies them.
verses.21:9: If the daughter of a priest is caught in fornication and violates the name of her father, she shall be burned up in flames.
verses.21:10: The high priest, that is, the greatest priest among his brothers, upon whose head the oil of anointing has been poured, and whose hands have been consecrated in the priesthood, and who has been clothed in the holy garments, shall not uncover his head nor tear his garments,
verses.21:11: and he shall not go in to any dead person at all; even for his father and mother he shall not be defiled.
verses.21:12: Nor shall he go out from the holy places, so that he does not pollute the sanctuary of the Lord, because the oil of the holy anointing of his God is upon him. I am the Lord.
verses.21:13: He shall take a virgin as a wife;
verses.21:14: however, he shall not take a widow, or a divorced woman, or a sordid woman, or a prostitute, but a young woman from his own people,
verses.21:15: so that he does not mingle the stock of his lineage with the common people of his nation, because I am the Lord who sanctifies him.'"
verses.21:16: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.21:17: "Speak to Aaron: 'A man from your seed throughout the families who has a blemish shall not offer loaves to his God,
verses.21:18: nor shall he approach His ministry: if he is blind, if lame, if with a small or a large or a crooked nose,
verses.21:19: if with a broken foot, or with a broken hand,
verses.21:20: if hunchbacked, if bleary-eyed, if having a white spot in the eye, if having chronic scabies, if having impetigo on the body, or if having a hernia.
verses.21:21: No one from the seed of Aaron the priest who has a blemish shall approach to offer sacrifices to the Lord, nor loaves to his God;
verses.21:22: yet he may eat of the loaves that are offered in the sanctuary,
verses.21:23: provided only that he does not enter within the veil, nor approach the altar, because he has a blemish and must not defile My sanctuary. I am the Lord who sanctifies them.'"
verses.21:24: Therefore Moses spoke to Aaron, and to his sons, and to all Israel, all the things that had been commanded to him.
verses.22:1: The Lord also spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.22:2: "Speak to Aaron and to his sons, that they beware of the things of the sons of Israel that have been consecrated, and do not defile the name of the things sanctified to Me, which they themselves offer. I am the Lord.
verses.22:3: Say to them, and to their descendants: 'Every man from your lineage in whom there is uncleanness, who approaches those things that have been consecrated and that the sons of Israel have offered to the Lord, shall perish before the Lord. I am the Lord.
verses.22:4: A man from the seed of Aaron who is leprous, or suffering a flow of seed, shall not eat of the things that have been sanctified to Me, until he is healed. He who touches one unclean because of a dead person, or he from whom seed goes out as in intercourse,
verses.22:5: or he who touches a creeping thing, or any unclean thing whose touch is foul,
verses.22:6: shall be unclean until evening, and shall not eat of the things that have been sanctified; but when he has washed his flesh with water,
verses.22:7: and the sun has set, then, having been cleansed, he shall eat of the sanctified things, because it is his food.
verses.22:8: They shall not eat what has died of itself or what has been caught by a beast, nor shall they be polluted by them. I am the Lord.
verses.22:9: Let them keep My precepts, so that they do not become subject to sin and die in the sanctuary when they have polluted it. I am the Lord who sanctifies them.
verses.22:10: No foreigner shall eat of the sanctified things; a tenant of a priest or a hired worker shall not eat of them.
verses.22:11: However, the one whom a priest has bought, and the one who is born in his house, these shall eat of them.
verses.22:12: If the daughter of a priest is married to anyone from the people, she shall not eat of the things that have been sanctified, nor of the firstfruits.
verses.22:13: But if, being a widow or divorced and without children, she has returned to the house of her father, just as she had been accustomed as a young woman, she shall be fed with the food of her father. No foreigner has the authority to eat of them.
verses.22:14: Whoever eats of the sanctified things through ignorance shall add a fifth part together with what he ate, and shall give it to the priest into the sanctuary.
verses.22:15: Nor shall they defile the sanctified things of the sons of Israel, which they offer to the Lord,
verses.22:16: so that they may not bear the iniquity of their offense when they eat the sanctified things. I am the Lord who sanctifies them.'"
verses.22:17: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.22:18: "Speak to Aaron and his sons, and to all the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them: 'Any man from the house of Israel, or from the sojourners who dwell among you, who offers his offering, whether fulfilling vows or offering freely, whatever he offers as a burnt offering to the Lord,
verses.22:19: so that it may be offered through you, it shall be an unblemished male from the cattle, or from the sheep, or from the goats;
verses.22:20: if it has a blemish, you shall not offer it, nor shall it be acceptable.
verses.22:21: A man who offers a sacrifice of peace offerings to the Lord, whether fulfilling vows or offering freely, whether from the cattle or from the sheep, shall offer an unblemished one so that it may be acceptable; no blemish shall be in it.
verses.22:22: If it is blind, if broken, if having a scar, if pustules, or scabies, or impetigo, you shall not offer them to the Lord, nor shall you burn any of them upon the altar of the Lord.
verses.22:23: An ox or a sheep with ear and tail cut off you may offer voluntarily, but a vow cannot be fulfilled from them.
verses.22:24: You shall not offer to the Lord any animal whose testicles are either crushed, or bruised, or cut and removed, and in your land do not do this at all.
verses.22:25: From the hand of a foreigner you shall not offer loaves to your God, nor anything else that he may wish to give, because they are all corrupted and blemished; you shall not accept them.'"
verses.22:26: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.22:27: "An ox, a sheep, and a goat, when they are born, shall be for seven days under the udder of their mother; but on the eighth day, and from then on, they may be offered to the Lord.
verses.22:28: Whether it is a cow or a sheep, they shall not be sacrificed on the same day with their young.
verses.22:29: If you sacrifice an offering for thanksgiving to the Lord, so that it may be pleasing,
verses.22:30: you shall eat it on the same day; nothing shall remain until the morning of the next day. I am the Lord.
verses.22:31: Keep My commandments, and do them. I am the Lord.
verses.22:32: Do not pollute My holy name, so that I may be sanctified in the midst of the sons of Israel. I am the Lord who sanctifies you,
verses.22:33: and brought you out of the land of Egypt, so that I might be God to you. I am the Lord."
verses.23:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.23:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you will say to them: 'These are the feast days of the Lord, which you will proclaim holy.
verses.23:3: For six days you will do work; the seventh day, because it is the rest of the sabbath, will be proclaimed holy; you will not do any work on it; it is a sabbath of the Lord in all your dwellings.
verses.23:4: These, therefore, are the holy feast days of the Lord, which you must celebrate in their seasons.
verses.23:5: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, is the Passover of the Lord;
verses.23:6: and on the fifteenth day of this month is the solemnity of unleavened bread of the Lord. For seven days you will eat unleavened bread.
verses.23:7: The first day will be most celebrated and holy for you; you will not do any servile work on it,
verses.23:8: but you will offer a sacrifice by fire to the Lord for seven days. The seventh day, however, will be more celebrated and holier; and you will do no servile work on it.'"
verses.23:9: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.23:10: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you will say to them: 'When you have entered the land which I will give to you, and have reaped the crop, you will bring sheaves of ears of grain, the firstfruits of your harvest, to the priest,
verses.23:11: who will lift up the bundle before the Lord, so that it may be acceptable for you, on the day after the sabbath, and he will sanctify it.
verses.23:12: And on the same day on which the sheaf is consecrated, an unblemished year-old lamb will be slaughtered as a burnt offering to the Lord.
verses.23:13: And libations will be offered with it, two-tenths of fine flour moistened with oil as a fire offering to the Lord and a most sweet aroma; offerings of wine also, a fourth part of a hin.
verses.23:14: You will not eat bread, parched grain, or porridge from the crop until the day on which you offer from it to your God. It is an everlasting precept in your generations and in all your dwelling places.
verses.23:15: Therefore you will count from the day after the sabbath, on which you offered the sheaf of the firstfruits, seven full weeks,
verses.23:16: until the day after the completion of the seventh week, that is, fifty days; and so you will offer a new sacrifice to the Lord
verses.23:17: from all your dwelling places, two loaves of firstfruits from two-tenths of leavened fine flour, which you will bake as firstfruits to the Lord.
verses.23:18: And you will offer with the loaves seven unblemished year-old lambs, and one calf from the herd, and two rams, and they will be for a burnt offering with their libations, for a most sweet aroma to the Lord.
verses.23:19: You will also prepare a male goat for sin, and two year-old lambs as victims of peace offerings.
verses.23:20: And when the priest has lifted them up with the loaves of firstfruits before the Lord, they will pass to his use.
verses.23:21: And you will proclaim this day most celebrated and most holy; you will not do any servile work on it. It will be an everlasting statute in all your dwelling places and your generations.
verses.23:22: Now after you have reaped the crop of your land, you will neither cut it down to the ground nor gather the remaining ears of grain; but you will leave them for the poor and the foreigners. I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.23:23: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.23:24: "Speak to the sons of Israel: 'In the seventh month, on the first day of the month, there will be for you a sabbath, a memorial, with trumpets sounding, and it will be proclaimed holy;
verses.23:25: you will not do any servile work on it, and you will offer a burnt offering to the Lord.'"
verses.23:26: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.23:27: "On the tenth day of this seventh month, the day of expiations will be most celebrated, and it will be proclaimed holy; and you will afflict your souls on it, and you will offer a burnt offering to the Lord.
verses.23:28: You will not do any servile work during the time of this day, because it is a day of propitiation, so that the Lord your God may be propitious to you.
verses.23:29: Every soul that has not been afflicted on this day will perish from its peoples;
verses.23:30: and the one that has done any work at all, I will blot it out from its people.
verses.23:31: Therefore you will do no work at all on it; it will be an everlasting statute for you in all your generations and your dwellings.
verses.23:32: It is a sabbath of rest, and you will afflict your souls on the ninth day of the month; from evening until evening you will celebrate your sabbaths."
verses.23:33: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.23:34: "Speak to the sons of Israel: 'From the fifteenth day of this seventh month, there will be the feast days of tabernacles for seven days to the Lord.
verses.23:35: The first day will be proclaimed most celebrated and most holy; you will not do any servile work on it.
verses.23:36: And for seven days you will offer burnt offerings to the Lord. The eighth day also will be most celebrated and most holy, and you will offer a burnt offering to the Lord, for it is a day of assembly and gathering; you will not do any servile work on it.
verses.23:37: These are the feast days of the Lord, which you will proclaim most celebrated and most holy, and you will offer on them oblations to the Lord, burnt offerings and libations according to the rite of each day,
verses.23:38: besides the sabbaths of the Lord, and your gifts, and what you will offer by a vow, or what you will give voluntarily to the Lord.
verses.23:39: From the fifteenth day of the seventh month, therefore, when you have gathered all the fruits of your land, you will celebrate the feast days of the Lord for seven days; on the first day and on the eighth day there will be a sabbath, that is, a rest.
verses.23:40: And you will take for yourselves on the first day fruits of the most beautiful tree, and fronds of palm trees, and boughs of a tree of dense foliage, and willows from the brook, and you will rejoice before the Lord your God.
verses.23:41: And you will celebrate His solemnity for seven days each year; it will be an everlasting statute in your generations. In the seventh month you will celebrate the festivals,
verses.23:42: and you will dwell in shaded shelters for seven days; everyone who is of the lineage of Israel will remain in tabernacles,
verses.23:43: so that your descendants may learn that I made the sons of Israel dwell in tabernacles when I brought them out from the land of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.23:44: And Moses spoke concerning the solemnities of the Lord to the sons of Israel.
verses.24:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying:
verses.24:2: "Command the sons of Israel to bring to you purest and clear oil from olives, to tend the lamps continually,
verses.24:3: outside the veil of the testimony in the tabernacle of the covenant. And Aaron will place them from evening until morning before the Lord, by a perpetual worship and rite in your generations.
verses.24:4: Upon the purest lampstand they will always be placed in the sight of the Lord.
verses.24:5: You will also take fine flour, and bake from it twelve loaves, which individually will contain two-tenths;
verses.24:6: you will set six of them on each side upon the purest table before the Lord;
verses.24:7: and you will place upon them the clearest frankincense, so that the bread may be for a memorial of the oblation to the Lord.
verses.24:8: On each sabbath they will be changed before the Lord, received from the sons of Israel by an everlasting covenant;
verses.24:9: and they will belong to Aaron and his sons, so that they may eat them in a holy place, because it is a holy of holies from the sacrifices of the Lord, by a perpetual right."
verses.24:10: Now look, the son of an Israelite woman, whom she had borne by an Egyptian man among the sons of Israel, went out and quarreled in the camp with an Israelite man.
verses.24:11: And when he had blasphemed the Name and cursed it, he was brought to Moses. (Now his mother was called Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, of the tribe of Dan.)
verses.24:12: And they put him in prison, until they knew what the Lord would command.
verses.24:14: saying: "Bring the blasphemer outside the camp, and let all who heard place their hands upon his head, and let the entire people stone him.
verses.24:15: And to the sons of Israel you will speak: 'A person who curses his God will bear his sin;
verses.24:16: and whoever blasphemes the name of the Lord, let him surely die; the entire multitude will overwhelm him with stones, whether he is a citizen or a foreigner. Whoever blasphemes the name of the Lord, let him surely die.
verses.24:17: Whoever strikes and kills a person, let him surely die.
verses.24:18: Whoever strikes an animal will repay a substitute, that is, life for life.
verses.24:19: Whoever inflicts a blemish upon any one of his citizens, just as he has done, so it will be done to him:
verses.24:20: fracture for fracture, eye for eye, tooth for tooth he will restore; whatever kind of blemish he has inflicted, such he will be compelled to endure.
verses.24:21: Whoever strikes a beast of burden will repay another. Whoever strikes a person will be punished.
verses.24:22: Let there be an equal judgment among you, whether a foreigner or a citizen has sinned, because I am the Lord your God.'"
verses.24:23: And Moses spoke to the sons of Israel; and they brought the one who had blasphemed outside the camp, and overwhelmed him with stones. And the sons of Israel did just as the Lord had commanded Moses.
verses.25:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying,
verses.25:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you shall say to them, 'When you have entered the land that I will give to you, you shall keep a sabbath to the Lord.
verses.25:3: For six years you shall sow your field, and for six years you shall prune your vineyard, and you shall gather its fruits;
verses.25:4: but in the seventh year there shall be a sabbath for the land, of the rest of the Lord: you shall not sow the field, and you shall not prune the vineyard.
verses.25:5: What the ground produces of its own accord you shall not reap, and the grapes of your firstfruits you shall not gather as a vintage, for it is a year of rest for the land;
verses.25:6: but they shall be for food to you: for you and your male servant, your female servant and your hired worker, and the strangers who sojourn with you;
verses.25:7: to your beasts of burden and livestock, everything that grows shall provide food.
verses.25:8: You shall also count for yourself seven weeks of years, that is, seven times seven, which together make forty-nine years;
verses.25:9: and you shall sound the trumpet in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, at the time of propitiation, throughout all your land.
verses.25:10: And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year, and proclaim release to all the inhabitants of your land, for it is the jubilee. A man shall return to his possession, and each one shall go back to his former family,
verses.25:11: because it is the jubilee and the fiftieth year. You shall not sow, nor shall you reap what grows of its own accord in the field, and you shall not gather the firstfruits of the vintage,
verses.25:12: on account of the sanctification of the jubilee, but you shall immediately eat what is presented.
verses.25:13: In the year of jubilee, all shall return to their possessions.
verses.25:14: When you sell anything to your fellow citizen, or buy from him, do not grieve your brother, but according to the number of years of the jubilee you shall buy from him,
verses.25:15: and according to the reckoning of the crops he shall sell to you.
verses.25:16: The more years that remain after the jubilee, the more the price shall also increase; and the less time you count, the less the purchase shall also cost, for he shall sell to you the time of the crops.
verses.25:17: Do not afflict your fellow tribesmen, but let each one fear his God, because I am the Lord your God.
verses.25:18: Do My precepts, and keep the judgments, and fulfill them, so that you may dwell in the land without any dread,
verses.25:19: and the ground may produce for you its fruits, which you may eat to fullness, fearing the attack of no one.
verses.25:20: And if you say, "What shall we eat in the seventh year, if we have not sown nor gathered our crops?"
verses.25:21: I will give My blessing to you in the sixth year, and it shall produce the fruits of three years;
verses.25:22: and you shall sow in the eighth year, and you shall eat the old crops until the ninth year; until the new grow, you shall eat the old.
verses.25:23: The land also shall not be sold in perpetuity, because it is Mine, and you are strangers and tenants of Mine;
verses.25:24: therefore the entire region of your possession shall be sold under the condition of redemption.
verses.25:25: If your impoverished brother sells his small possession, and his near relative is willing, he may redeem what the other had sold.
verses.25:26: But if he does not have a next of kin, and he himself is able to find the price to redeem it,
verses.25:27: the fruits shall be calculated from the time when he sold it, and what remains he shall pay back to the buyer, and thus he shall recover his possession.
verses.25:28: But if his hand does not find enough to pay back the price, the buyer shall hold what he had bought until the jubilee year. For in that year every sale shall return to the owner and to the former possessor.
verses.25:29: Whoever sells a house within the walls of a city shall have the right to redeem it until one year is completed.
verses.25:30: If he does not redeem it, and the cycle of the year has elapsed, the buyer shall possess it, and his descendants in perpetuity, and it will not be able to be redeemed, even in the jubilee.
verses.25:31: But if a house is in a village that has no walls, it shall be sold by the law of fields; if it has not been redeemed beforehand, in the jubilee it shall return to the owner.
verses.25:32: The houses of the Levites that are in the cities may always be redeemed;
verses.25:33: if they have not been redeemed, in the jubilee they shall return to the owners, because the houses of the cities of the Levites are in place of possessions among the sons of Israel.
verses.25:34: But their outlying lands shall not be sold, because it is a perpetual possession.
verses.25:35: If your brother becomes impoverished and weak in hand, and you receive him as a stranger and a sojourner, and he lives with you,
verses.25:36: do not take interest from him, nor more than you gave; fear your God, so that your brother may live with you.
verses.25:37: You shall not give your money to him at interest, and you shall not demand a surplus of crops.
verses.25:38: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, so that I might give you the land of Canaan and be your God.
verses.25:39: If, compelled by poverty, your brother sells himself to you, you shall not oppress him with the servitude of slaves,
verses.25:40: but he shall be like a hired worker and a tenant; until the jubilee year he shall work with you,
verses.25:41: and afterward he shall go out with his children, and return to his kindred, to the possession of his fathers.
verses.25:42: For they are My servants, and I brought them out of the land of Egypt; they shall not be sold under the condition of slaves;
verses.25:43: do not afflict him by force, but fear your God.
verses.25:44: Let your male slave and female slave be from the nations that are around you;
verses.25:45: and from the strangers who sojourn among you, or those who have been born from them in your land, these you shall have as slaves;
verses.25:46: and by hereditary right you shall hand them down to your descendants and possess them forever; but do not oppress your brothers, the sons of Israel, by force.
verses.25:47: If the hand of a stranger and sojourner grows strong among you, and your impoverished brother sells himself to him, or to anyone of his lineage,
verses.25:48: after the sale he may be redeemed. Whoever wishes from among his brothers shall redeem him,
verses.25:49: and a paternal uncle, and a paternal cousin, and a blood relative, and a relative by marriage. But if he himself is also able, he shall redeem himself,
verses.25:50: provided only that the years are reckoned from the time of his sale until the jubilee year, and the money for which he had been sold is reckoned according to the number of years and the rate of a hired worker.
verses.25:51: If there are more years that remain until the jubilee, according to these he shall also pay back the price;
verses.25:52: if few, he shall make a reckoning with him according to the number of years, and he shall pay back to the buyer what remains of the years,
verses.25:53: with the wages for which he previously served being credited; he shall not afflict him violently in your sight.
verses.25:54: But if he cannot be redeemed by these means, in the jubilee year he shall go out with his children.
verses.25:55: For the sons of Israel are My servants, whom I brought out of the land of Egypt.'"
verses.26:1: "I am the Lord your God: you must not make for yourselves an idol or a carved image, nor erect memorial pillars, nor place a marked stone in your land so that you may worship it. For I am the Lord your God.
verses.26:2: Keep My Sabbaths, and stand in awe before My sanctuary. I am the Lord.
verses.26:3: If you walk in My precepts, and keep My commandments and do them, I will give you rains in their seasons,
verses.26:4: and the land will bring forth its produce, and the trees will be filled with fruit.
verses.26:5: The threshing of the harvests will overtake the grape harvest, and the grape harvest will reach the sowing; and you will eat your bread to satisfaction, and you will dwell without dread in your land.
verses.26:6: I will give peace within your borders; you will sleep, and there will be no one to terrify you. I will remove evil beasts, and the sword will not cross your boundaries.
verses.26:7: You will pursue your enemies, and they will collapse before you.
verses.26:8: Five of your own will pursue a hundred foreigners, and a hundred of you ten thousand; your enemies will fall by the sword in your sight.
verses.26:9: I will look upon you and make you grow; you will be multiplied, and I will confirm My covenant with you.
verses.26:10: You will eat the oldest of the old, and as the new arrives you will throw out the old.
verses.26:11: I will set My tabernacle in your midst, and My soul will not reject you.
verses.26:12: I will walk among you, and I will be your God, and you will be My people.
verses.26:13: I am the Lord your God, who brought you out from the land of the Egyptians so that you would not serve them, and who shattered the chains on your necks so that you might walk upright.
verses.26:14: But if you do not listen to Me, nor do all My commandments,
verses.26:15: if you spurn My laws and hold My judgments in contempt, so that you do not do the things that have been established by Me, and bring My covenant to nothing:
verses.26:16: I also will do these things to you: I will visit you swiftly with want, and with burning fever that will wear out your eyes and consume your souls. In vain you will sow seed, which will be devoured by foes.
verses.26:17: I will set My face against you, and you will collapse before your foes, and you will be subjected to those who hate you; you will flee with no one pursuing.
verses.26:18: But if even so you do not obey Me, I will increase your chastisements sevenfold because of your sins,
verses.26:19: and I will crush the pride of your hardness. And I will give you a sky above like iron, and a bronze earth.
verses.26:20: Your labor will be consumed in vain; the land will not bring forth produce, nor will the trees yield fruit.
verses.26:21: If you walk in opposition to Me and are unwilling to listen to Me, I will increase your plagues sevenfold because of your sins;
verses.26:22: and I will send the beasts of the field among you, which will consume you and your livestock and reduce all things to a few, and your roads will become deserted.
verses.26:23: And if even so you are unwilling to accept discipline, but walk in opposition to Me,
verses.26:24: I also will advance against you in opposition, and I will strike you seven times because of your sins,
verses.26:25: and I will bring upon you a sword avenging My covenant. And when you take refuge in the cities, I will send pestilence into your midst, and you will be handed over into the hands of foes,
verses.26:26: after I have broken the staff of your bread, so that ten women bake loaves in one oven and hand them back by weight; and you will eat, and will not be satisfied.
verses.26:27: But if even through these things you do not listen to Me, but walk against Me,
verses.26:28: then I too will advance against you in opposing fury, and I will chastise you with seven plagues because of your sins,
verses.26:29: so that you eat the flesh of your sons and of your daughters.
verses.26:30: I will destroy your high places, and shatter the images. You will fall among the ruins of your idols, and My soul will abhor you,
verses.26:31: to such an extent that I will reduce your cities to desolation, and make your sanctuaries deserted, and no longer accept the sweetest aroma.
verses.26:32: And I will lay waste your land, and your enemies will be astonished over it when they become its inhabitants.
verses.26:33: You, however, I will scatter among the nations, and I will unsheathe the sword after you, and your land will be deserted, and your cities demolished.
verses.26:34: Then its Sabbaths will please the land all the days of its desolation; when you are
verses.26:35: in a hostile land, it will keep Sabbath and rest during the Sabbaths of its desolation, because it did not rest during your Sabbaths when you were dwelling in it.
verses.26:36: And as for those of you who remain, I will put dread into their hearts in the regions of foes; the sound of a flying leaf will terrify them, and they will flee as though from a sword; they will fall with no one pursuing,
verses.26:37: and each will collapse upon his brothers, as though fleeing battles; none of you will dare to resist enemies.
verses.26:38: You will perish among the nations, and a hostile land will consume you.
verses.26:39: And if some of these also remain, they will waste away in their iniquities in the land of their enemies, and because of the sins of their fathers and their own they will be afflicted,
verses.26:40: until they confess their iniquities and those of their ancestors, by which they transgressed against Me and walked in opposition to Me.
verses.26:41: Therefore I also will walk against them, and I will bring them into a hostile land, until their uncircumcised mind is ashamed; then they will pray for their impieties.
verses.26:42: And I will remember My covenant which I made with Jacob, and Isaac, and Abraham. I will also be mindful of the land,
verses.26:43: which, when it has been abandoned by them, will delight itself in its Sabbaths, enduring desolation because of them. But they themselves will plead for their sins, because they rejected My judgments and despised My laws.
verses.26:44: And yet even when they were in a hostile land, I did not utterly reject them, nor did I so despise them that they would be consumed and make My covenant with them void. For I am the Lord their God,
verses.26:45: and I will remember My former covenant, when I brought them out from the land of Egypt in the sight of the nations, so that I might be their God. I am the Lord." These are the judgments and precepts and laws which the Lord gave between Himself and the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai by the hand of Moses.
verses.27:1: And the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,
verses.27:2: "Speak to the sons of Israel, and you will say to them, 'A person who makes a vow and pledges his soul to God will give the price according to an assessment.
verses.27:3: If it is a male from the twentieth year up to the sixtieth year, he will give fifty shekels of silver by the measure of the sanctuary;
verses.27:5: And from the fifth year up to the twentieth, a male will give twenty shekels; a female, ten.
verses.27:6: From one month up to the fifth year, for a male five shekels will be given; for a female, three.
verses.27:7: At sixty years old and older, a male will give fifteen shekels; a female, ten.
verses.27:8: If he is poor and is not able to pay the assessment, he will stand before the priest; and as much as the priest assesses and sees that he is able to pay, that much he will give.
verses.27:9: Now if anyone vows an animal that can be sacrificed to the Lord, it will be holy,
verses.27:10: and it cannot be exchanged, that is, neither a better one for a bad one, nor a worse one for a good one; but if he does exchange it, both the very one that has been exchanged and the one for which it has been exchanged will be consecrated to the Lord.
verses.27:11: If anyone vows an unclean animal that cannot be sacrificed to the Lord, it will be brought before the priest,
verses.27:12: who, judging whether it is good or bad, will set the price.
verses.27:13: And if the one who offers wishes to pay, he will add a fifth part above the assessment.
verses.27:14: If a person vows his house and sanctifies it to the Lord, the priest will examine it, whether it is good or bad, and according to the price that has been fixed by him, it will be sold;
verses.27:15: but if the one who had vowed wishes to redeem it, he will give a fifth part of the assessment in addition, and he will have the house.
verses.27:16: And if he vows a field of his possession and consecrates it to the Lord, the price will be assessed according to the measure of the seed: if the land is sown with thirty modii of barley, let it be sold for fifty shekels of silver.
verses.27:17: If he vows the field immediately from the year when the jubilee begins, it will be assessed at as much as it can be worth.
verses.27:18: But if it is after some time, the priest will calculate the money according to the number of the years that remain until the jubilee, and a deduction will be made from the price.
verses.27:19: And if the one who had vowed wishes to redeem the field, he will add a fifth part of the assessed money, and he will possess it.
verses.27:20: However, if he does not wish to redeem it, but it has been sold to any other person, the one who had vowed will no longer be able to redeem it.
verses.27:21: Because when the day of jubilee comes, it will be sanctified to the Lord, and the consecrated possession belongs by right to the priests.
verses.27:22: If a field that was bought, and is not from the possession of ancestors, has been sanctified to the Lord,
verses.27:23: the priest will calculate the price according to the number of years until the jubilee, and the one who had vowed it will pay it to the Lord.
verses.27:24: And in the jubilee it will return to the former owner, who had sold it and had held it in the allotment of his possession.
verses.27:25: Every assessment will be weighed by the shekel of the sanctuary. A shekel has twenty obols.
verses.27:26: No one will be able to sanctify and vow the firstborn, which belong to the Lord; whether it is an ox or a sheep, they are the Lord's.
verses.27:27: And if the animal is unclean, the one who offered it will redeem it according to your assessment, and will add a fifth part of the price; if he does not wish to redeem it, it will be sold to another for whatever amount it has been assessed by you.
verses.27:28: Everything that is consecrated to the Lord, whether it is a person, or an animal, or a field, will not be sold, nor can it be redeemed. Whatever has once been consecrated will be a holy of holies to the Lord;
verses.27:29: and every consecration that is offered by a person will not be redeemed, but will surely die.
verses.27:30: All the tithes of the land, whether from the crops or from the fruits of the trees, are the Lord's, and are sanctified to Him.
verses.27:31: And if anyone wishes to redeem his tithes, he will add a fifth part of them.
verses.27:32: Of all the tithes of ox and sheep and goat that pass under the shepherd's rod, whatever comes tenth will be sanctified to the Lord.
verses.27:33: Neither a good one nor a bad one will be chosen, nor will it be exchanged for another; if anyone exchanges it, both what has been exchanged and that for which it has been exchanged will be sanctified to the Lord, and will not be redeemed.'"
verses.27:34: These are the precepts that the Lord commanded Moses for the sons of Israel on Mount Sinai.

notes.1:1: Vulgate reads "tabernaculo testimonii" ("tabernacle of the testimony"), matching the Greek Septuagint, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "tent of meeting."
notes.1:3: Vulgate reads "ad placandum sibi Dominum" ("to make the Lord favorable to himself"), where the Hebrew reads "for his acceptance before the Lord."
notes.1:8: Here and in 1:12, the Vulgate specifies "all that adheres to the liver" ("quae adhaerent jecori"), whereas the Hebrew reads simply "the fat" (suet).
notes.1:15: Vulgate "retorto ad collum capite, ac rupto vulneris loco" ("with its head twisted back to the neck and the place of the wound broken open") gives a detailed procedural rendering of the Hebrew verb for wringing off the bird's head; "crepidinem" denotes the projecting ledge or base of the altar.
notes.1:17: Latin "ascellas" denotes the bird's wing-joints or wings, and "neque ferro dividet eam" ("nor divide it with iron") is a Vulgate clarification of the Hebrew prohibition against severing the bird completely.
notes.2:1: Vulgate preserves the literal "Anima" ("a soul," rendering Hebrew "nefesh") for the offerer and translates Hebrew "minchah" ("grain offering") simply as "sacrificium" ("sacrifice") throughout chapter 2.
notes.2:2: Vulgate reads "ponet" ("shall place") for the memorial on the altar, whereas the Hebrew specifies burning it in smoke.
notes.2:5: Vulgate renders the two cooking utensils of verses 5 and 7 as "sartago" ("frying pan") and "craticula" ("grill" or "gridiron"), whereas the Hebrew refers to a flat griddle and a deep pan.
notes.2:14: Latin "far" (here and in 2:16 "farris fracti") denotes coarse, husked grain or groats, contrasting with "simila" ("fine flour") in verses 1-7.
notes.3:5: Vulgate reads "in holocaustum" ("as a burnt offering"), whereas the Hebrew reads "upon the burnt offering" already on the altar.
notes.3:6: Vulgate renders the Hebrew term for a mixed flock of sheep and goats simply as "de ovibus" ("from the sheep"), even though verse 12 goes on to prescribe the offering of a goat.
notes.3:10: Vulgate connects "caudam totam" (3:9) with "cum renibus" ("the entire tail with the kidneys"), whereas the Hebrew states that the fat tail is removed "close to the backbone."
notes.3:15: Compared with 3:4 and 3:10, the Vulgate here exchanges the anatomical terms, placing "reticulum" ("membrane") over the kidneys beside the flanks and "arvina" ("fat") on the liver.
notes.4:2: Latin anima ("soul") is used throughout Leviticus 4-5 as a literal biblical idiom for an individual person.
notes.4:4: Vulgate tabernaculi testimonii ("tabernacle of the testimony") follows the Septuagint tradition, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "tent of meeting."
notes.4:20: Throughout Leviticus 4-5, the Vulgate renders the priest's atoning act with verbs of intercessory prayer (rogare and orare, "pray," joined with expians in 5:13), and here reads propitius erit eis Dominus ("the Lord will be merciful to them") where the Hebrew has "it will be forgiven them."
notes.4:35: Vulgate arietis ("ram") is a distinctive reading where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "lamb" and the Septuagint "sheep."
notes.5:2: Vulgate quod occisum a bestia est, aut per se mortuum ("what was killed by a beast, or died on its own") differs from the Hebrew list of unclean animal carcasses, and oblita fuerit ("forgets") here and in verses 3-4 renders the Hebrew "it is hidden from him."
notes.5:5: Vulgate agat poenitentiam ("let him repent") is a distinctive Latin rendering; the Hebrew Masoretic Text and Septuagint speak of confessing the sin.
notes.5:15: Vulgate qui emi potest duobus siclis ("which can be bought for two shekels") specifies a two-shekel price reflecting ancient Jewish legal tradition, whereas the Hebrew mentions a valuation in "shekels of silver" without stating the number two.
notes.5:20: In this versification (matching the Hebrew Masoretic Text), Leviticus 5 continues through 5:26; other versifications number 5:20-26 as 6:1-7.
notes.6:1: In this versification (matching the Hebrew Masoretic Text), chapter 6 begins here; other versifications number this verse 6:8.
notes.6:4: Vulgate distinctly adds "usque ad favillam consumi faciet" ("will cause them to be consumed down to fine ash"), distinguishing coarse charred ashes ("cineres", v. 3) from fine ash ("favillam"). Clementine "efferret" is an orthographic variant of future indicative "efferet".
notes.6:10: Vulgate "quia pars ejus in Domini offertur incensum" ("because part of it is offered as a fire offering of the Lord") differs from MT ("I have given it as their portion from My fire offerings"). Here and in 7:5, 25, Latin "incensum" (literally "what is kindled/burned") denotes a fire offering on the altar, distinct from "thus" ("frankincense", v. 8), and "Sanctum sanctorum" is literally "holy of holies" (a superlative idiom).
notes.6:14: Vulgate "calidam" ("hot") reflects a distinct reading from MT ("well-mixed" / "baked pieces"), and v. 15 "qui jure patri successerit" ("who succeeds his father by right") renders MT's "anointed priest in his place."
notes.7:10: Unlike MT (which opens v. 10 as a new sentence beginning "And every grain offering"), the Vulgate links v. 10 directly to v. 9, shifting from plural "conspersa ... arida fuerint" to singular "dividetur."
notes.7:20: Vulgate renders Hebrew "be cut off" as "peribit" ("will perish"; likewise "interibit" in v. 21 and "peribit" in vv. 25, 27) and preserves the plural "de populis suis" ("from its peoples") in vv. 20, 21, and 27, contrasting with singular "de populo suo" ("from his people") in v. 25.
notes.7:24: Vulgate ends v. 24 at "habebitis in varios usus" ("you will have for various uses"), omitting MT's concluding prohibition ("but you shall by no means eat it"), and renders Hebrew "torn" as "captum" ("caught").
notes.7:34: Vulgate distinctly names the priestly portions "pectusculum elevationis" ("breast of elevation") and "armum separationis" ("shoulder of separation", using "armus" = shoulder/forequarter rather than MT "thigh", also in vv. 32-33), and in v. 29 adds the explanatory gloss "id est, libamenta ejus" ("that is, its libations").
notes.7:38: Clementine "mandabit" is a Late Latin b/v spelling for perfect "mandavit" ("commanded"), as shown by the past-sequence subjunctive "ut offerrent." In v. 37, Clementine punctuation connects "sacrificii" directly with "pro peccato atque delicto" rather than setting it off as a separate item in the list.
notes.8:8: The Vulgate uses humerale ("shoulder-vestment", v. 7) for the Hebrew ephod, rationale ("breastpiece", from Latin ratio, reflecting Greek logeion) for the breastpiece of judgment, and Doctrina et Veritas ("Doctrine and Truth") for the Hebrew Urim and Thummim. Syntactically, the Vulgate fits the shoulder-vestment (quod) to the breastpiece (rationali).
notes.8:16: Latin reticulum jecoris literally denotes the net-like membrane (caul or omentum) of the liver, where the Hebrew refers to the appendage or lobe of the liver.
notes.8:25: Latin armo dextro ("right shoulder", as also in 8:26 and 9:21) follows the Septuagint against the Hebrew "right thigh." Similarly, in 8:27, 8:29, and 9:21, the Vulgate uses verbs of lifting up (levaverunt / elevans) where the Hebrew specifies a wave offering.
notes.8:34: The Vulgate reads "just as has also been done at the present time, so that the rite of the sacrifice might be completed," where the Hebrew reads "As has been done this day, the Lord has commanded to do, to make atonement for you."
notes.9:7: Where the Hebrew twice uses the verb for "make atonement," the Vulgate renders the first instance as deprecare ("intercede") and the second as ora ("pray").
notes.9:16: The Vulgate condenses the end of 9:15 and all of 9:16 into "when the altar had been purified, he made the burnt offering," omitting the Hebrew references to offering the sin offering like the first and performing the burnt offering according to the ordinance.
notes.9:17: Latin libamenta ("libations") stands where the Hebrew specifies a grain offering taken by the handful and burned on the altar.
notes.9:23: Latin tabernaculum testimonii ("the tabernacle of the testimony") follows the Septuagint rendering of the Hebrew "tent of meeting." In 9:24, the Vulgate also reads "they praised the Lord" where the Hebrew reads "they shouted."
notes.10:5: The Vulgate explicitly reads "just as they lay, clothed in linen tunics" (sicut jacebant, vestitos lineis tunicis) and "cast them outside" (ejecerunt foras), whereas the Hebrew simply says they carried them out "by their tunics."
notes.10:9: The Vulgate renders Hebrew "strong drink" descriptively as "anything that can intoxicate" (omne quod inebriare potest), and renders the "tent of meeting" as "tabernacle of the testimony" (tabernaculum testimonii), following the Septuagint.
notes.10:14: The Vulgate reads "shoulder" (armum) for the Hebrew thigh/leg, "in a most clean place" (in loco mundissimo, superlative), and "sacrifices of salvation" (hostiis salutaribus), echoing the Septuagint's rendering of peace/fellowship offerings.
notes.10:18: The Vulgate reads "as was commanded to me" (sicut praeceptum est mihi), agreeing with the Septuagint, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "as I commanded."
notes.10:19: The Vulgate renders Aaron's closing question distinctively as "or please the Lord in the ceremonies with a mournful mind?" (mente lugubri), whereas the Hebrew asks whether eating the sin offering would have pleased the Lord; in 10:20, recepit satisfactionem literally means "accepted satisfaction," i.e., accepted Aaron's justification.
notes.11:4: The Vulgate adds "and the rest" (et cetera) after the camel; in 11:5 choerogryllus (from Greek choirogryllios) denotes the rock hyrax.
notes.11:13: In 11:13-19 the Vulgate follows the Septuagint's Greek bird names, yielding several renderings that differ from the Hebrew, including "griffin" (gryphem, understood in antiquity as a giant vulture or bird of prey), "ostrich" (struthionem), "ibis" (ibin), "swan" (cygnum), and "purple gallinule" (porphyrionem).
notes.11:22: The Vulgate borrows three Greek locust-type terms (bruchus, a wingless locust; attacus and ophiomachus, leaping locust species whose exact identities remain uncertain) before locusta ("locust"), in a different sequence from the Hebrew.
notes.11:29: In 11:29-30 the Vulgate again follows the Septuagint's fauna names, rendering crocodilus ("crocodile," used in antiquity for a large land lizard/monitor), mygale ("shrew"), and stellio ("spotted lizard" or gecko); in 11:35, chytropodes (literally "pot-feet") denotes footed clay cooking pots or pot-stands.
notes.11:42: The Vulgate distinctively combines "on its breast on four feet" (super pectus quadrupes graditur) and concludes with "or drags itself along the ground" (sive per humum trahitur), whereas the Hebrew lists belly-crawlers, four-footed walkers, and many-footed creatures separately; in 11:47 the Vulgate uses second-person verbs ("so that you may know..."), keeping 11:46-47 within the Lord's direct speech.
notes.12:2: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew verb for conceiving (literally 'produces seed') as the passive ablative absolute suscepto semine ('after receiving seed').
notes.12:3: The Vulgate reads simply 'the little infant shall be circumcised' (circumcidetur infantulus), omitting the explicit reference to 'the flesh of his foreskin' found in the Hebrew and Septuagint.
notes.12:6: Following the Septuagint, the Vulgate renders Hebrew 'tent of meeting' as 'the tabernacle of the testimony' (tabernaculi testimonii). Latin pro peccato literally means 'for sin', corresponding to the Hebrew term for a sin offering.
notes.12:7: Here and in verse 8, the Vulgate translates the Hebrew verb for making atonement as 'pray for her' (orabit pro ea), and renders Hebrew 'the fountain of her blood' as 'the discharge of her blood' (a profluvio sanguinis sui).
notes.12:8: Latin non invenerit manus ejus ('her hand does not find [enough]') preserves a literal Hebraism for lacking the means to provide a lamb, which the Vulgate clarifies with the following clause.
notes.13:3: Vulgate "ad arbitrium ejus separabitur" ("at his decision he will be separated") differs from the Hebrew, which reads "pronounce him unclean." Throughout this chapter, the Vulgate also renders the depth of a lesion with "humilior" ("lower") rather than "deeper."
notes.13:11: Biblical Latin uses "contaminabit" (literally "will defile") and "mundabit" (13:6, literally "will cleanse") declaratively to mean "will pronounce unclean" and "will pronounce clean" throughout this chapter.
notes.13:13: Vulgate "teneri lepra mundissima judicabit" ("will judge him to be held by a most clean leprosy") is a distinctive Vulgate wording where the Hebrew states simply that the priest shall pronounce the affliction clean.
notes.13:25: Vulgate "versa est in alborem" ("it has turned to whiteness") takes the scar as its subject without mentioning hair, whereas the Hebrew specifies that the hair in the bright spot has turned white.
notes.13:31: Vulgate "et capillum nigrum" ("and the hair black") omits the negation found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, which reads "and there is no black hair in it."
notes.13:45: Vulgate renders this verse with distinctive wording: "vestimenta dissuta" ("unstitched garments"), "os veste contectum" ("his mouth covered with a garment," vs. Hebrew "upper lip"), and indirect speech "contaminatum ac sordidum se clamabit" ("will cry out that he is defiled and filthy," vs. Hebrew "Unclean, unclean!").
notes.13:49: Vulgate reads "alba vel rufa" ("white or red") where the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads "greenish or reddish."
notes.13:57: Vulgate "lepra volatilis et vaga" ("a flying and wandering leprosy") is a distinctive rendering of the Hebrew term for a spreading eruption, and "in those places that were previously unspotted" replaces the Hebrew list of garment and leather parts.
notes.14:4: Throughout this chapter (vv. 4-7, 49-53), the Vulgate renders the generic Hebrew term for birds specifically as 'passeres' ("sparrows"), and here translates "clean" as 'quibus vesci licitum est' ("that it is lawful to eat").
notes.14:10: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew liquid measure 'log' with the Roman unit 'sextarius' (roughly a pint; also in vv. 12, 15, 21, 24) and omits "of an ephah" after "three tenths of fine flour."
notes.14:20: Here and in v. 31, the Vulgate has 'libamentis' ("libations" or drink offerings) where the Hebrew text refers to the grain offering ('minchah').
notes.14:31: Unlike v. 22 ('pro peccato', "for sin") and the Hebrew text of v. 31 ("sin offering"), the Clementine Vulgate reads 'pro delicto' ("for trespass") and omits the closing atonement clause; elsewhere in the chapter (vv. 19, 21, 29, 53), it translates Hebrew "make atonement" variously as 'rogare' ("pray"), 'placare' ("appease"), and 'orare' ("pray").
notes.14:56: The phrase 'et in varias species, coloribus immutatis' ("and when the colors have been changed into various appearances") is a Vulgate-distinct addition not found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text, while v. 57 omits the Hebrew's concluding line ("This is the law of leprosy").
notes.15:2: Vulgate "fluxum seminis" ("a flow of seed") specifies a seminal discharge, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text reads more generally "a discharge from his flesh."
notes.15:3: Vulgate "when moment by moment a foul fluid clings to his flesh and congeals" is a distinctly clinical Latin rendering of the Hebrew clause describing a discharge that either runs or is stopped up.
notes.15:10: Vulgate omits the verb "touches" found in the Hebrew and Greek texts here, stating directly that whatever has been beneath the man is defiled until evening.
notes.15:22: Latin "vas" (literally "vessel" or "utensil") is used broadly in the Vulgate for any household article or furnishing. The Vulgate divides Hebrew 15:19 into two verses, so its 15:21-23 correspond to Hebrew 15:20-22; it has no counterpart to Hebrew 15:23.
notes.16:1: Vulgate "when they were killed while offering strange fire" explicitly recalls the incident of Leviticus 10:1, whereas the Hebrew reads "when they drew near before the Lord and died."
notes.16:2: Throughout this chapter the Vulgate alternates between "propitiatorium" ("mercy seat", vv. 2, 14) and "oraculum" ("oracle", vv. 2, 13, 15) to render the single Hebrew term for the cover of the ark.
notes.16:8: Vulgate "capro emissario" ("for the emissary goat") interprets Hebrew "la'azazel" ("for Azazel") as a goat designated to be sent away; see also verses 10 and 26.
notes.16:10: Vulgate "ut fundat preces super eo" ("so that he may pour out prayers over it") renders the Hebrew verb for making atonement in terms of intercessory prayer, a distinctive Vulgate pattern also reflected in verses 6, 11, 17, 18, 24, and 34.
notes.16:18: Vulgate "oret pro se" ("let him pray for himself") differs from the Hebrew, which speaks of making atonement for the altar itself.
notes.17:4: The Vulgate softens the Hebrew declaration 'he has shed blood' into a comparison, 'quasi si sanguinem fuderit' ('as if he had shed blood'), and uses the active 'peribit' ('he shall perish') where the Hebrew has passive 'shall be cut off.'
notes.17:5: The Vulgate reads 'ut sanctificentur Domino' ('so that they may be sanctified to the Lord') rather than the Hebrew 'that they may bring them to the Lord,' and follows the Septuagint in rendering 'tent of meeting' as 'tabernaculum testimonii' ('tabernacle of the testimony').
notes.17:7: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew goat-demons or satyrs ('se'irim') simply as 'dæmonibus' ('demons') and 'throughout their generations' as 'et posteris eorum' ('and for their descendants').
notes.17:11: Latin 'anima' encompasses both 'life' and 'soul' across this verse. The closing clause 'et sanguis pro animæ piaculo sit' ('and that the blood may be for the expiation of the soul') is a Vulgate-distinct rendering compared with the Hebrew 'for it is the blood that makes atonement by the life.'
notes.17:14: The Vulgate reads 'in sanguine est' ('is in the blood') twice here, echoing verse 11, where the Hebrew states that the life of all flesh 'is its blood.'
notes.18:6: Throughout verses 6-19, the Vulgate avoids anatomical 'nuditas' ('nakedness') for Hebrew 'ervah,' translating it with 'turpitudo' ('shame/indecency') and varying it with 'ignominia' ('disgrace,' vv. 15, 17) and 'fœditas' ('foulness,' v. 19). Latin 'proximam sanguinis sui' explicitly specifies a close female blood relative.
notes.18:14: Where the Hebrew states 'she is your aunt,' the Vulgate renders 'quæ tibi affinitate conjungitur' ('who is joined to you by marriage,' using the Roman legal term 'affinitas' for relationship by marriage).
notes.18:17: The Vulgate specifies 'uxoris tuæ' ('your wife') rather than Hebrew 'a woman,' and renders Hebrew 'depravity/wickedness' explicitly as 'et talis coitus incestus est' ('and such intercourse is incest').
notes.18:21: Where the Hebrew speaks of causing offspring to 'pass over' (commonly understood as passing through fire) to Molech, the Vulgate reads 'ut consecretur idolo Moloch' ('to be consecrated to the idol Molech').
notes.18:25: The Vulgate expresses 'ut evomat' as a purpose or result clause ('so that it may vomit out its inhabitants') rather than the Hebrew statement that the land already vomited them out; similarly, in verse 28 the Vulgate reads 'cum paria feceritis' ('when you do like things') where the Hebrew has 'when you defile it.'
notes.19:9: Vulgate reads 'non tondebis usque ad solum superficiem terræ' (not shearing the surface of the land all the way to the ground), whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text forbids reaping to the edges or corners of the field.
notes.19:18: Vulgate here uses 'amicum tuum' ('your friend'), where vv. 13 and 16 render the same Hebrew noun with forms of 'proximus' ('neighbor').
notes.19:20: Vulgate describes the slave woman as 'etiam nubilis' ('even of marriageable age') and prescribes 'vapulabunt ambo' ('both shall be beaten'), whereas the Hebrew text refers to a slave woman designated for a man and states that there shall be an inquiry or punishment.
notes.19:23: Vulgate renders the idiom literally as 'auferetis præputia eorum' ('you shall remove their foreskins') and omits the phrase 'for three years' found in the Hebrew text, though 'the fourth year' follows in v. 24.
notes.19:36: Vulgate uses the Roman units 'modius' (a dry measure) and 'sextarius' (a liquid or dry measure) to render the Hebrew 'ephah' and 'hin'.
notes.20:11: Vulgate uses 'noverca' ('stepmother') here for Hebrew 'father's wife', and throughout vv. 11-21 renders the Hebrew idiom 'nakedness' with the moral terms 'turpitudo' ('shame') and 'ignominia' ('disgrace').
notes.20:14: Vulgate reads 'vivus ardebit cum eis' ('he shall burn alive with them'), explicitly specifying burning alive, whereas the Hebrew text states that they shall burn him and them with fire.
notes.20:20: Vulgate expands Hebrew 'his uncle' to 'patrui vel avunculi sui' ('his paternal uncle or his maternal uncle') and reads 'cognationis suæ' ('of his relatives') where Hebrew reads 'of his uncle'.
notes.20:24: Vulgate opens with a present-tense statement and imperative ('Vobis autem loquor. Possidete'), whereas the Hebrew text uses past narration followed by a future verb ('I said to you, You shall inherit').
notes.20:27: Vulgate 'pythonicus spiritus' ('a pythonic spirit') is a Greco-Roman term derived from the Pythian oracle at Delphi, used here for a spirit of mediumship or necromancy.
notes.21:4: Latin "sed nec in principe populi sui contaminabitur" ("but not even for a ruler of his people shall he be defiled") renders a difficult Hebrew clause (literally "a husband/chief shall not defile himself among his people, so as to profane himself") as a prohibition against defilement even for a deceased ruler.
notes.21:8: The Vulgate specifies "panes propositionis" ("the loaves of presentation") and maintains third-person plural verbs, whereas the Hebrew refers more generally to "the bread of your God" in the second person singular.
notes.21:10: Latin "Pontifex, id est, sacerdos maximus" incorporates Jerome's explanatory gloss ("that is, the greatest priest"), and "caput suum non discooperiet" ("shall not uncover his head") renders a Hebrew verb commonly understood as leaving the hair disheveled.
notes.21:15: Latin "ne commisceat stirpem generis sui vulgo gentis suae" ("so that he does not mingle the stock of his lineage with the common people of his nation") is a distinctly Vulgate rendering where the Hebrew reads "so that he does not profane his offspring among his people."
notes.21:18: The Vulgate's "si parvo vel grandi, vel torto naso" ("if with a small or a large or a crooked nose") interprets two Hebrew terms for a disfigured face/nose and an oversized limb as three nasal defects; similarly in v. 20, "lippus" ("bleary-eyed") corresponds to a Hebrew term usually taken to mean a dwarf or withered person.
notes.22:2: The Vulgate's "nomen sanctificatorum mihi" ("the name of the things sanctified to Me") attaches "name" directly to the consecrated offerings, whereas the Hebrew warns against profaning "My holy name" regarding what the Israelites consecrate.
notes.22:9: Latin "in sanctuario" ("in the sanctuary") explicitly names the sanctuary where the Hebrew has the pronoun "in it" (or "because of it"), referring to the priestly charge or sacred offerings.
notes.22:10: Latin "alienigena" (literally "foreigner" or "one of another stock") is used here and in v. 13 for any layperson outside the priestly household, the same Latin word used in v. 25 for a non-Israelite foreigner.
notes.22:19: The Vulgate's "ut offeratur per vos" ("so that it may be offered through you") is a distinctly Vulgate reading where the Hebrew means "for your acceptance" (that it may be accepted on your behalf).
notes.22:23: Latin "aure et cauda amputatis" ("with ear and tail cut off") is a distinctive Vulgate rendering of two Hebrew terms generally understood to describe an animal with an elongated or stunted limb.
notes.23:8: The Vulgate uses comparative adjectives (celebrior et sanctior, "more celebrated and holier") for the seventh day, contrasting with the first day's "most celebrated and holy" (23:7), where the Hebrew uses the same phrase ("holy convocation") for both days.
notes.23:11: The Vulgate adds "and he will sanctify it" (et sanctificabit illum), a clause not found in the Hebrew Masoretic Text.
notes.23:13: The Vulgate uses libamenta ("libations") for the accompanying offering of fine flour moistened with oil (Hebrew minchah, grain offering), and liba vini ("offerings of wine") for the drink offering.
notes.23:22: The Vulgate reads "you will neither cut it down to the ground" (nec secabitis eam usque ad solum), whereas the Hebrew prohibits harvesting the edge or corner of the field.
notes.23:36: The Vulgate renders the closing assembly with a doubled genitive phrase, est enim cœtus atque collectæ ("for it is a day of assembly and gathering"), where the Hebrew has a single term for a solemn assembly.
notes.24:2: The Vulgate specifies "purest and clear oil" (purissimum, ac lucidum) and "to tend the lamps" (ad concinnandas lucernas), where the Hebrew reads "pure beaten olive oil" to keep a lamp burning.
notes.24:8: The Vulgate reads mutabuntur ("they will be changed"), referring to the weekly replacement of the twelve loaves, where the Hebrew verb means to arrange them.
notes.24:18: The Vulgate adds the clarifying phrase vicarium, id est ("a substitute, that is") before "life for life" (animam pro anima).
notes.24:21: The Vulgate translates the penalty for striking a person with the general term punietur ("will be punished"), whereas the Hebrew explicitly specifies capital punishment ("shall be put to death").
notes.25:2: The Latin text reads second-person singular sabbatizes ("you shall keep a sabbath"), anticipating the singular address of verse 3, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text (and some Latin witnesses reading sabbatizet) makes the land the subject ("the land shall keep a sabbath").
notes.25:5: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew term for unpruned or consecrated vines (nazir) as uvas primitiarum tuarum ("the grapes of your firstfruits"; compare primitias vindemiae, "the firstfruits of the vintage," in verse 11).
notes.25:12: The Latin statim oblata comedetis ("you shall immediately eat what is presented") refers to eating directly what the land yields without harvesting and storing it, rendering the Hebrew "you shall eat its produce from the field."
notes.25:35: In the Vulgate syntax, "and you receive him ... and he lives with you" remains part of the conditional clause leading into the prohibition of verse 36, whereas the Hebrew makes "you shall uphold him" the main command of verse 35.
notes.25:53: The Vulgate renders the opening clause as quibus ante servivit mercedibus imputatis ("with the wages for which he previously served being credited"), differing from the Hebrew "like a hired worker year by year he shall be with him."
notes.26:1: The Clementine Vulgate opens this verse with "I am the Lord your God" (Ego Dominus Deus vester), framing the verse with a double divine self-declaration where the Hebrew Masoretic Text has this formula only at the end; it also uses the plural titulos ("memorial pillars") and insignem lapidem ("marked stone").
notes.26:16: Where the Hebrew Masoretic Text lists sudden terror, wasting disease, and fever, the Vulgate renders the first term adverbially as velociter ("swiftly") and translates the affliction as egestate, et ardore ("want, and ... burning fever"), with the masculine relative qui referring specifically to ardore.
notes.26:41: The Vulgate distinctively reads donec erubescat incircumcisa mens eorum ("until their uncircumcised mind is ashamed") and tunc orabunt pro impietatibus suis ("then they will pray for their impieties"), differing from the Hebrew "if their uncircumcised heart is humbled and they make amends for their iniquity" (compare rogabunt in v. 43).
notes.26:44: The Vulgate uses past tenses throughout this verse and a third-person plural verb facerent ("and make My covenant with them void"), making Israel rather than God the grammatical subject of voiding the covenant.
notes.26:45: The Clementine Vulgate includes the concluding colophon ("These are the judgments...") within verse 45, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text numbers it separately as verse 46.
notes.27:13: The Vulgate reads dare voluerit (literally "wishes to give," i.e., pay the assessed price to keep the animal), whereas the Hebrew text specifies "wishes to redeem it."
notes.27:16: The Vulgate renders the Hebrew homer as triginta modiis ("thirty modii," a Roman dry measure of about a peck each) and reads venundetur ("let it be sold," as in v. 14 venundabitur) where the Hebrew refers to the valuation itself.
notes.27:25: The Vulgate uses obolos ("obols," a Greco-Latin weight and coin unit following the Septuagint) corresponding to the Hebrew gerah.
notes.27:29: The Vulgate translates the Hebrew term for a thing under the ban (cherem) with consecratio ("consecration"), renders it as quæ offertur ab homine ("that is offered by a person," rather than "devoted from among humans"), and uses the active emphatic idiom morte morietur (literally "will die by death") where the Hebrew has a passive verb ("be put to death").
notes.27:32: The Vulgate specifies bovis et ovis et capræ ("ox and sheep and goat") and adds pastoris ("the shepherd's" rod), where the Hebrew reads more generally "of herd and flock" and simply "under the rod."
